key_insight: A2M shows that MCP agents can be hijacked in a black-box way by first increasing tool selection through crafted metadata and then steering outcomes with trace-informed malicious returns.
engineering_relevance: The work highlights a practical supply-chain security risk for agentic tool ecosystems and motivates stronger tool vetting, isolation, and runtime monitoring.
method: Attraction: optimize attacker-controlled tool metadata to maximize invocation probability.
Manipulation: use execution traces to iteratively refine adversarial tool outputs.
Black-box framework: targets MCP agents without needing model internals.
evidence_signal: On LiveMCPBench, the method achieved 93.6% malicious tool invocation on GLM-4.6, 74.4% mean attack success across three attack goals, and up to 32.4× benign token cost under denial-of-service settings.
watch_item: Results depend on attack optimization against specific benchmark scenarios, so transferability and real-world robustness may be lower than the reported direct-attack performance.
paper_title: A2M: Trace-Optimized Agent Hijacking in the MCP Ecosystem
